source_span: For three years, the AI trade had a lender of last resort, and it sold GPUs. That lender just lost its chairman. ... that's roughly half a trillion dollars of contingent and committed cash for a company that generates $50-60 billion of free cash flow a quarter.
source_chain: Jensen Huang personally drove Nvidia's $530.5B of financing commitments/guarantees/buybacks (incl. the $105B Ohio/OpenAI backstop) that recycle its $50-60B/quarter FCF back into AI-ecosystem buyers, therefore his exit pauses the willingness/ability to write new deals (UBS: could pull ~$50B+ out of the system just as rates rise and credit tightens), therefore the banks split on severity (Goldman: existing deals honored, next round harder, PT cut to $220 from $300, Buy kept; JPM credit: Underweight, continued spread weakness; Piper Sandler: investment case unchanged, $300 PT kept) — invalidated/tested by whether the $500B financing platform (zero deals in 3 months, earliest Jan 2027) stays open to new deals going forward.
pulse_chain: Jensen Huang resigned, therefore UBS's $50-60B/quarter spare cash recycled into AI financing could see a pause pulling $50B+ out of the system as borrowing costs rise, therefore banks split (Goldman cuts target to $220 from $300 keeping Buy, expects every commitment honored but the next round harder; JPM Underweight the credit, expects new deals to take longer/cost more; Piper Sandler keeps $300 target, says CEO change doesn't alter the case) — invalidated/tested by Kress's Nov 17 earnings as the first read on whether the $500B platform (zero deals in three months, earliest Jan 2027) stays open to new deals.
why: The pulse reproduces the source's lending mechanism, the same direction and figures for each named bank (UBS's $50-60B/quarter, Goldman's $220/$300 target cut with Buy kept, JPM credit's Underweight, Piper Sandler's unchanged $300 case), and the same platform-deal invalidation condition, with no reversed step or swapped attribution.
